title: Relative Tor intervals under Tor-independent base change of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and tensor pullback computed by K-flat resolutions [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Say that $f$ and $g$ are Tor independent when, for every compatible pair of geometric points $\bar x$ of $X$ and $\bar y'$ of $Y'$ over $\bar y$ of $Y$, one has $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}}_i(\mathcal O_{X,\bar x},\mathcal O_{Y',\bar y'})=0$ for all $i>0$, with Tor computed by projective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Assume this Tor independence; it holds in particular whenever $f$ is flat, meaning flat on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. If $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$, then $L(g')^*E$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $(f')^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y'}$. Here amplitude over a ring sheaf means that derived tensor with every module sheaf in degree zero has cohomology zero outside $[a,b]$. The assertion holds for each fixed pair of integers $a\le b$ and hence etale locally with locally chosen intervals. Neither pseudo-coherence nor local finite presentation nor flatness of $g$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0DKD (lemma-tor-independence-and-tor-amplitude), clause (1), with the target inverse-image ring corrected from the printed f to f-prime; Tor independence definition Tag 08IP (definition-tor-independent). The flat case is immediate from flat geometric stalk rings, spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04NG (lemma-flat-at-point-etale-local-rings), and vanishing of higher Tor for a flat module.

proof.text: First check the stated sufficient hypothesis. If $f$ is flat, [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness] says that every structural geometric stalk ring $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ is flat over $R=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$. For any compatible $B=\mathcal O_{Y',\bar y'}$, take a projective resolution of $B$ as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Tensoring its exact augmented sequence with $A$ preserves exactness at each positive degree by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Thus $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(B,A)=0$ for $i>0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] gives $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A,B)=0$. The remaining steps use only this Tor independence, not flatness of $f$.

Fix a geometric point $\bar x'$ of $X'$ and its images $\bar x,\bar y',\bar y$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y',\bar y'}$, $C=\mathcal O_{X',\bar x'}$, and $D=A\otimes_R B$. Write $M=E_{\bar x}$ as an $A$-complex. By [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative], the stalk of an inverse image at a geometric point is the stalk at the image point, compatibly with the ring structures; hence $(f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_{\bar x}=R$, and similarly $((f')^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y'})_{\bar x'}=B$, acting on $C$ through the stalk map of $f'$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-ring-sheaf-tor-amplitude-stalk-test] to the ring sheaf $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$: $M$, restricted to $R$, has amplitude $[a,b]$. By [lem-sfb-space-geometric-stalk-tensor-calculus], $D\to C$ is flat and $(L(g')^*E)_{\bar x'}\simeq M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C$ in $D(C)$. In particular we retain $C$; we do not identify it with $D$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-point ringed site to choose an $A$-K-flat resolution $Q\to M$, and an $R$-K-flat resolution $P\to Q|_R$. The latter also represents $M|_R$. Tor independence and [lem-pc-tor-independent-kflat-resolution-tensor] give a quasi-isomorphism $B\otimes_R P\to B\otimes_R Q$ of $B$-complexes. Put $T=D\otimes_A Q$. The generator formula of [lem-pc-base-tensor-ordinary-iso] identifies $T|_B$ with $B\otimes_R Q$. By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], $B\otimes_R P$ represents $M|_R\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B$ in $D(B)$. Thus $T|_B$ represents precisely that scalar extension, with its $B$-action; no boundedness of $Q$ or flatness of $B/R$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 0661, lemma-base-change-comparison, free-resolution calculation, and Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution.

proof.text: The forward direction of [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model], over $R$, provides a flat complex $L$ supported in $[a,b]$ representing $M|_R$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat] on the one-point ringed space. Therefore [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] identifies $T|_B$ in $D(B)$ with $B\otimes_R L$. Each $B\otimes_R L^j$ is flat over $B$: for an exact sequence of $B$-modules, restrict to $R$, use [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] for $L^j$, and identify $N\otimes_B(B\otimes_R L^j)$ with $N\otimes_R L^j$ by $n\otimes(b\otimes l)\mapsto bn\otimes l$, inverse $n\otimes l\mapsto n\otimes(1\otimes l)$. Its terms vanish outside $[a,b]$. The reverse direction of [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model], now over $B$, proves that $T|_B$ has amplitude $[a,b]$. This is the flat-model proof of ordinary scalar-extension preservation, written here as an application of existing nodes.

source.place: Tag 066L, lemma-pull-tor-amplitude, proof using Tag 0654, lemma-tor-amplitude; cohomology.tex Tag 06YD, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat.

proof.text:
Let $N$ be an arbitrary $B$-module in degree zero and choose a $B$-K-flat resolution $F\to N[0]$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Form $V=\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_B F)$ with the $D$-action through $T$. The mixed restriction comparison [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-restriction-comparison] and the fixed-second-factor derived construction [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] show that $V|_B$ represents $T|_B\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N$. (The usual signed flip interchanges the two homogeneous factors, with sign $(-1)^{pq}$.) Hence $H^i(V)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, since forgetting a module action leaves its kernels and images unchanged. Apply [new-lem-pc-mixed-total-tensor-scalar-extension] with its rings $(R,A,Aq)=(B,D,C)$ and complexes $(Q,F)=(T,F)$. After the mixed restriction identifications this is the $C$-linear chain isomorphism
$$C\otimes_D V\ \cong\ \operatorname{Tot}((C\otimes_D T)\otimes_B F),$$
sending $c\otimes(t\otimes u)$ to $(c\otimes t)\otimes u$. The right side, restricted to $B$, represents $(C\otimes_D T)|_B\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N$ by the same fixed-second-factor construction. This uses a chain isomorphism already stated in the DAG, not an assumed mixed derived associativity theorem.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change, fixed-second-factor construction; mixed rebracketing on total complexes as in Tag 08YU, lemma-double-base-change.

proof.text: For $i\notin[a,b]$, the three consecutive terms $V^{i-1}\to V^i\to V^{i+1}$ are exact at $V^i$. Since $C$ is flat over $D$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] makes their tensors with $C$ exact there as well. Thus $H^i(C\otimes_D V)=0$; step 5 gives the required vanishing against every $N$. Finally $C\otimes_D T=C\otimes_D(D\otimes_A Q)\cong C\otimes_A Q$, by $c\otimes(d\otimes q)\mapsto cd\otimes q$, inverse $c\otimes q\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes q)$. Since $Q$ is $A$-K-flat, this last complex computes $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C$ by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. Consequently the stalk of $L(g')^*E$ has amplitude $[a,b]$ over $B$. Apply the converse of [lem-sfb-space-ring-sheaf-tor-amplitude-stalk-test] to the ring sheaf $(f')^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y'}$ on $X'$ to obtain the asserted global interval. The same criterion applies on every etale chart, so applying the argument on the inverse images of charts carrying an input interval gives the locally chosen intervals. Empty charts and the empty space cause only vacuous stalk conditions. All test modules were arbitrary; no pseudo-coherence, finite presentation or flatness of $g$ entered.
